steps.title: Two main types
steps.body: Formal letters (to officials, businesses, newspapers) and Informal letters (to friends and family). The exam usually requires formal letters.

steps.title: Salutations
steps.body: Dear Mr/Mrs/Ms [Surname] - if you know the name Dear Sir/Madam - if you don't know the name To the Editor - for letters to newspapers

steps.title: Sign-offs
steps.body: "Yours sincerely" - if you used a name (Dear Mr Smith) "Yours faithfully" - if you used Dear Sir/Madam

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: In exams, you're almost always asked to write a formal letter. Avoid contractions and slang. Use sophisticated vocabulary appropriately.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: When should you use "Yours faithfully" versus "Yours sincerely"? | What is the correct order for a formal letter's components? | Write the opening of a letter to your local council about litter in your area.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: "Yours faithfully" with Dear Sir/Madam; "Yours sincerely" when using a specific name (Dear Mr Smith). | Sender's address, date, recipient's address, salutation, content, sign-off, signature. | Your opening should include: sender's address, date, council's address, "Dear Sir/Madam", and a clear statement of purpose.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always check if formal or informal is required Set out addresses correctly - they're easy marks Never use contractions in formal letters Match your sign-off to your salutation State your purpose clearly in the first paragraph Use persuasive techniques appropriate to your purpose Keep paragraphs focused - one main idea each
